fields.name: summary
fields.value:
YieldShield Alpine is an Avalanche-specific Fuji prototype for seven-day AVAX protection. Holders deposit test AVAX and choose either an AVAX exit under gain-sharing terms or surrender the whole position for separately reserved Alpine Demo Dollar backing. Junior providers supply first-loss capital and receive acquired AVAX and gain-sharing fees. Unclosed positions settle for their entry backing at maturity; holders must exit before then to retain upside. Junior entry and withdrawal pause while positions are active to keep accounting fair.

The dedicated interface is live at https://avalanche.yieldshield.ai. Contracts are ready for Fuji deployment but await faucet test AVAX; we do not claim a live Fuji pool. Engineering evidence includes 14 passing contract tests with 256 fuzz cases, exact-unit arithmetic tests, responsive browser checks and a signed 13-transaction LOCAL lifecycle. Local activity is not onchain adoption. Live reference reads use Chainlink AVAX/USD on Fuji; synthetic scenarios are isolated. aDEMO is a project-issued valueless test token, not Circle USDC.

The implementation is AI-assisted and unaudited. No external-user, revenue, real TVL or organic-volume metrics are claimed. We request funding only for additional Avalanche work beyond this existing prototype. No YieldShield token launch or mainnet release is included.

The source repository is currently private. The public website provides the demo and its deployment status.

fields.name: milestones
fields.value:
Six weeks after acceptance; $10,000 total for approximately 100 hours of additional implementation, verification and product work at a blended $100/hour. Today’s prototype is prior work and is not billed.

1. Integration hardening, weeks 1–2, $4,000: add native-USDC/WAVAX adapter checks, expand oracle/expiry stress cases beyond the existing suite, publish a scoped threat model and reserve monitoring. Acceptance evidence: verified token identities, failure-mode tests and reproducible results.

2. Independent testnet pilot, weeks 3–4, $3,000: recruit 10 consenting independent testers, observe 30 complete journeys across both exits and junior claims, record usability failures, and improve accessibility and recovery. These are future targets, not current traction.

3. Release and handoff, weeks 5–6, $3,000: resolve material pilot findings, publish Avalanche integration examples and release notes, deliver USDC/WAVAX readiness and sAVAX decision reports, and establish a 30-day monitoring/handoff plan.

No double billing with other grants. Mainnet rollout, liquidity incentives and comprehensive external audit are excluded. Any overlapping funding would be disclosed and the scope repriced before acceptance.

fields.name: why_grant
fields.value:
YieldShield brings a focused, testable risk-allocation primitive to Avalanche rather than requiring a new L1 or incentive token. The proposal makes the key questions inspectable: what backing is reserved, who bears losses, what can be withdrawn, and what happens at expiry. The mini-grant would fund Avalanche-specific hardening and independent pilot evidence, with a clear route to native USDC/WAVAX integrations. BENQI sAVAX remains research until its redemption delays, market value and liquidity can be handled correctly.

We are David Hawig and Santiago Balaguer, operating through Hawig Ventures UG (haftungsbeschränkt), Germany. David is Founder/Managing Director and works full-time on YieldShield; he previously served as Director of Ecosystem at Web3 Foundation and founded and exited two startups. Santiago is Cofounder/Product Lead, with 15 years of product experience and five years in crypto.
David: https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-hawig-206a44b1/
Santiago: https://www.linkedin.com/in/santiagobalaguer/

Our Base, Monad and BNB prototypes provide prior product learning; Alpine has a separate repository, deployment identity and Avalanche-specific scope. We are self-funded and have received no grants or investment, confirmed 11 October 2026. AI assistance is disclosed, and neither an external audit nor production safety is claimed.
